StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single, and this is the one unit in the on_stack family that goes the OTHER way: the sim does NOT override on_stack, so a second application adds. That happens to be what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236), so it is *more* faithful than the 15 units that override it to `pass` -- but it is still a gap, because C#'s AfterApplied fires only on a genuinely new power while the sim's __init__-time Minion grant (powers.py:1562-1564) likewise only runs on construction. Dormant: nothing reads Illusion's Amount, and the sim's stacking path (cmds.py:308-322) would not re-run __init__ anyway. Recorded so the inconsistency between this unit and its 15 siblings is visible.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE HOOK NOW EXISTS AND THIS POWER IMPLEMENTS IT: `hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death` is consulted by `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:67-83, called from the real-death arm at cmds.py:50), and `IllusionPower.should_power_be_removed_on_death` (powers.py:1647-1656) reproduces IllusionPower.cs:59-66 -- keep buffs, drop non-temporary debuffs -- with `getattr(power, 'is_temporary', False)` standing in for the still-absent ITemporaryPower marker. WHAT REMAINS is that it is unreachable for the case it was written for: an Illusion's own death takes the PREVENTION arm (powers.py:1671 `should_die` -> False), which never calls `_strip_powers_after_death`. So the LIVE debuff half is unchanged -- an Eye with Teeth given Vulnerable 3 and killed still revives holding it. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:30-83 and powers.py.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# grants MinionPower 1 from AfterApplied unless the owner already has it (IllusionPower.cs:68-75, applier null, cardSource null); the sim does it in __init__ with the same `"minion" not in owner.powers` test (powers.py:1562-1564) and the same absent applier. The sim has no AfterApplied slot, and __init__ runs at exactly the point PowerCmd.apply creates the power (cmds.py:324-327) -- i.e. BEFORE hooks.on_power_applied rather than after, which is the only difference and is unobservable because no ported listener reacts to a Minion grant. Named per the main report's section 7 item 6: the mechanism is __init__-for-AfterApplied, and it would break for any AfterApplied body that needs the power to already be registered.

AfterDeath.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. CLOSED: consequence (1) -- the prevention arm no longer floors HP, so an Illusion is dead at 0 and retained (cmds.py:51-64 sets `retained_after_death = True`), which is C#'s observable; and consequence (4) -- `hooks.on_death` fires on both arms with `was_removal_prevented` (hooks.py:799-811), so Gremlin Horn pays out. WHAT REMAINS: powers.py:1671-1675 still implements this via `should_die` returning False, so the sim takes the prevention arm where IllusionPower.cs:79's body sits behind `!wasRemovalPrevented` -- the flag is inverted for every listener, and the prevention arm skips `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:50), which is the ONLY caller of this power's own ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath port. The REVIVE_MOVE splice (IllusionPower.cs:83-88) is still absent: the sim leaves the revive to the owner's take_turn calling `revive()` (powers.py:1682-1686). Re-verified against cmds.py, hooks.py and powers.py.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: PowerCmd.apply now opens with `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return` (cmds.py:394-395), the sim's port of PowerCmd.Apply<T>'s `if (!target.CanReceivePowers) return null` (PowerCmd.cs:73-76), whose CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading cmds.py:369-396 and both C# files. WAS: the predicate was wired into DamageCmd.deal only, so a debuff landed on a creature the game refuses to touch -- Vulnerable sticking to a reviving Test Subject.

guards.issue: A public settable property with no sim analogue: it lets an applier choose which state the revived creature resumes on, defaulting to the last LOGGED state. Folded into the AfterDeath entry; carried separately because it survives a should_die-to-AfterDeath fix. Dormant, but NOT for the reason recorded before the 2026-07-26 fix pass ("no ported applier", which was false): both ported appliers have single self-looping move machines (Parafright.cs:44-47, EyeWithTeeth.cs:39-42) and neither sets FollowUpStateId, so the default resolves to the only state there is. Trigger: an IllusionPower applier with more than one move state, or a caller that sets the property.

guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE FLOOR IS GONE: `_resolve_death`'s prevention arm (cmds.py:51-64) no longer writes `target.hp = 1`; it leaves the creature dead at 0 HP, sets `retained_after_death = True`, fires `on_death(..., True)` and then `after_preventing_death` -- CreatureCmd.cs:560-571's shape. The 1-vs-0 HP number conformance asserts on now matches, and the downstream consequences this entry listed go with it (Feed's `if target.is_dead` scores, and steam_eruption's HP restore no longer depends on the floor -- it moved to `on_death`, powers.py:2144-2151). WHAT REMAINS: the sim still does not model C#'s RE-ENTRY. CreatureCmd.cs:562-565 re-enters `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` while `creature.IsDead`, up to 10 times before throwing InvalidOperationException; `_resolve_death`'s else-arm simply returns. So a prevention that heals nothing is permanent in the sim and re-kills in the game, and the sim still cannot express a prevention that fails. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:30-64.

Consequence (a) is moot as well: steam_eruption's 999999999 HP restore moved off `on_damage_received` onto `on_death` (powers.py:2144-2151), which this path fires. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading cmds.py:30-64 and :284-292.
